_note: Two-tier detection poller smoke test (~15-20 min). A short fast_timeout_s (120s) hands still-unseen keys to the SLOW tier instead of dropping them; the slow tier re-sweeps every 300s up to 4 passes and records true-but-late deliveries into deliverability.csv (never detection.csv). Confirm during/after the run: detection.csv holds fast-tier hits with first_fetched_at (propagation), deliverability.csv (if any key needed the slow tier) holds slow-tier hits with swept_at and NO first_fetched_at column, the dashboard/analyze deliverability is the union of the two while propagation stays detection-only. sweep_interval_s is shortened to 300s here so the slow tier exercises within a short run; production matrices use ~900s. Set sweep_max_passes=0 to disable the slow tier (legacy single-tier behaviour). Deliverability ground truth still comes from the offline resweep: resweep.py results/<run>. Re-derive offline with: analyze.py results/<run> --deliver-window-s 300
